method_notes: Two tasks. (1) THE CAMROSE: established current physical and operational truth from the club's own Save The Camrose account, Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's 11 February 2025 Cabinet report (read in full as a PDF, not summarised from search), the developer's own press release and the planning agent's project page. (2) HIGH-VALUE NO-CALENDAR RECOVERY: the 116 no-calendar venues were derived programmatically - every venue in venues.json whose venue_census_id appears in no record of calendar-sources.json - then segmented strictly by the required priority order: tier 1 proven principal capacity >= 10,000 by joining capacity-evidence.json on venue_census_id where is_principal is true (only 3 venues qualify); tier 2 INDOOR_ARENA and MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX of any size (9); tier 3 CONFERENCE_CENTRE, CONVENTION_CENTRE, EXHIBITION_CENTRE and CONFERENCE_EXHIBITION_COMPLEX (9); tier 4 THEATRE, CONCERT_HALL and AUDITORIUM at >= 1,500 by principal capacity or largest_room_capacity (12); tier 5 motorsport circuits and greyhound stadiums with expected published schedules (7). All 40 venues in tiers 1-5 were attempted; the 76 remaining venues (mostly sub-1,500 Northern Irish, Scottish and Welsh non-league football grounds and county cricket outgrounds) were deliberately not attempted, as instructed. Third-party ticket marketplaces (Ticketmaster, Skiddle, Ents24, Songkick, See Tickets, TicketSource, Resident Advisor, Live Nation) were excluded as source truth throughout; operator platforms tied to a specific venue (Academy Music Group, Trafalgar Entertainment, Spedeworth, a students' union box office) were accepted as first-party and recorded with the venue-specific URL. events_currently_present is true only where named forthcoming dated events were actually seen. Where a plain fetch returned a JavaScript shell on a venue that justified the cost, a real browser was used and the result is stated explicitly in the note (The Forum Bath, HERE at Outernet, Cheshire Oaks Arena, Leeds Town Hall). Where a site returned 403 or failed DNS and nothing could be read, the outcome is SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED or OFFICIAL_SITE_MISSING rather than a guess.

camrose_finding.reasoning: The census carries The Camrose as OPERATIONAL purely on the strength of an old Wikipedia capacity row; the current evidence contradicts that decisively, and the correct status is DERELICT. Basingstoke Town F.C.'s own site states the club was evicted in April 2019, that the ground is 'currently unused, vandalised and left to rot', that the freehold passed to Basron Developments in 2016 and that planning permission for housing and a care home was granted on appeal on 6 May 2022; the club has rented the Hampshire FA ground at Winklebury since October 2020. Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's Cabinet report of 11 February 2025 (The Camrose - disposal of council owned land and removal from list of Assets of Community Value) is decisive on the physical question and settles DERELICT over both DEMOLISHED and OPERATIONAL. Para 2.4: 'The original stands, terraces and hard standing areas associated with its previous use for footballing purposes still remain, although are proposed to be demolished. The use of the site as a football ground ceased before 2019.' Para 4.5: 'The current structures on the site are deteriorating and unsightly and are no longer fit for their original or indeed any other purpose.' Para 10.2: 'the site has not been fit for purpose for some time.' So the structures were still standing as at February 2025 - it is NOT demolished - but the site has not functioned as a venue since 2019. Redevelopment is consented and progressing but not built: outline permissions 19/01110/OUT (85 dwellings) and 19/02889/OUT (70-bed care home plus 6 dwellings) were both allowed on appeal in May 2022, each expressly 'following the demolition of the existing buildings and structures on the site'; a demolition prior-notification application 24/00047/DEM was determined on 2 February 2024; Sovereign Housing Developments acquired the freehold of the main site in December 2024 and the council resolved to sell its adjoining 29% and to strike the site from the Assets of Community Value list because 'there is no longer a realistic prospect of a future community use of the Camrose site as it will be developed out for affordable housing'. Para 7.1 anticipated a planning application later in 2025 and commencement of works in 2026, and the Sovereign Hill Partnership subsequently consulted in October 2025 on a revised scheme of circa 100 affordable homes, working towards a planning application in early 2026. I could NOT find evidence that demolition has actually taken place, so DEMOLISHED and REDEVELOPED are both unproven and are not claimed. DERELICT is the precise status: structures extant, unused, vandalised and deteriorating, sold for housing, ACV removed. NO_LONGER_EVENT_VENUE is equally true but less specific, and it is entailed by DERELICT. The venue should also lose OPERATIONAL status in the census and its operator field reviewed - Basingstoke Town F.C. has not occupied this ground since 2019.
camrose_finding.historical_capacity_note: The 6,000 figure must be RETAINED, not deleted, and re-labelled as HISTORICAL rather than current. It is a genuine record of the ground's spectator capacity while in football use up to 2019 and remains the correct historical value; the single capacity-evidence record for ukmec-england-basingstoke-the-camrose (is_principal true, 6000, SPECTATOR, GRADE_C, MEDIUM confidence, sourced from the Wikipedia List of football stadiums in England) should be kept but marked historical, with capacity_observed_at understood as an inherited list value rather than a 2026 observation. The defect to correct is not the number but the inference drawn from it: the venue is carried as OPERATIONAL merely because a capacity source exists. A capacity figure evidences past scale, never present operation. Going forward the figure should not be treated as a live spectator capacity, and it must not on its own requalify the site for CAPACITY_THRESHOLD_MET inclusion as an operational venue.

evidence.note: Basingstoke Town F.C.'s own Save The Camrose page. Proved the club's eviction and the ground's abandonment in the operator's own words: Rafi Razzak 'evicted the newly formed Community Club from The Camrose in April 2019'; 'The Camrose Stadium across the town is currently unused, vandalised and left to rot by ex-Chairman Rafi Razzak'; 'In 2016, whilst Rafi Razzak was Chairman and owner of the football club, the freehold of The Camrose land was purchased by Basron Developments, also owned by Rafi Razzak'; 'May 6th 2022 - The National Planning Inspectorate informed the community club that despite our fight, permission has been granted for Basron's housing and care home on the land of The Camrose'; and that 'Since October 2020 the Community Club has been renting the shared Hampshire FA ground at Winklebury Football Complex in Basingstoke'. Establishes that the named operator does not use this ground.

Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council, REPORT TO CABINET, 11 February 2025, 'The Camrose-disposal of council owned land and removal from list of Assets of Community Value'. Retrieved and read in full as a 13-page PDF. This is the decisive evidence and is what distinguishes DERELICT from DEMOLISHED. Para 2.4 proves the structures still stand and that venue use has ceased: 'The original stands, terraces and hard standing areas associated with its previous use for footballing purposes still remain, although are proposed to be demolished. The use of the site as a football ground ceased before 2019.' Para 4.5 proves dereliction: 'The current structures on the site are deteriorating and unsightly and are no longer fit for their original or indeed any other purpose.' Para 10.2 adds 'the site has not been fit for purpose for some time. Basingstoke Town Football Club has been playing at Hampshire FA in Winklebury.' Paras 2.6-2.8 give the consents: outline applications 19/01110/OUT (85 dwellings) and 19/02889/OUT (70-bed care home and 6 dwellings), both allowed on appeal in May 2022, each 'following the demolition of the existing buildings and structures on the site'. Para 2.10 records demolition prior-notification 24/00047/DEM determined on 2 February 2024. Para 3 of the Background records that 'In December 2024, SHD acquired the freehold interest of the former Camrose site'. Para 6.9 justifies ACV removal: 'there is no longer a realistic prospect of a future community use of the Camrose site as it will be developed out for affordable housing'. Para 6.5 notes the ACV listing was due to expire on 5 October 2025. Para 7.1 sets the timetable: disposal completed by late spring 2025, 'A planning application is expected later in 2025, and commencement of works in 2026.' Para 9.1: the land 'currently remains vacant and undeveloped'.

Sovereign Network Group's own press release (published 20 January 2025) on its purchase of the site on 17 December 2024. Independently corroborates the council report from the new freeholder's side and confirms the site is treated as former and derelict: it refers throughout to the 'former Camrose Stadium site', describes the site as derelict, and states 'The site, which has been vacant for some time, currently has planning permission for 85 homes and a 70-bedroom care home.' Confirms the buyer's identity and that redevelopment had not yet begun.

Planning agent Bell Cornwell's own project page for the redevelopment. Corroborates the consent position from the applicant's side: 'Two outline planning permissions secured for up to 95 dwellings and a 70 bed care home', allowed by the Planning Inspectorate after a four-day public inquiry following the local Planning Committee's refusal against officer recommendation, and records that Basingstoke Town F.C. secured an alternative permanent home at the upgraded Winklebury Football Complex. Confirms the ground's football use was formally replaced elsewhere rather than retained.

evidence.value: Why DERELICT rather than DEMOLISHED, REDEVELOPED or OPERATIONAL
evidence.note: OPERATIONAL is excluded: the site has hosted no football since 2019 (council para 2.4), the operator plays elsewhere (club site; council para 10.2), and the council formally removed the ACV on the basis that no community use remains realistic (para 6.9). DEMOLISHED is NOT asserted because no retained evidence shows demolition has actually occurred: the last direct physical statement (council, February 2025) is that the stands and terraces 'still remain', and demolition is consistently described in the future tense ('proposed to be demolished', 'SHD are expected to cover demolition costs'). REDEVELOPED is NOT asserted because the consented scheme was still unbuilt - a fresh planning application for a revised circa-100-home scheme was only being worked towards in early 2026 following an October 2025 consultation, and works were anticipated to commence in 2026. No source was found confirming either demolition or construction on the ground, and none was invented. DERELICT captures exactly what is proven: structures extant but unused, vandalised and deteriorating, freehold sold for housing, ACV removed. If a later probe evidences actual demolition, the status should move to DEMOLISHED; that evidence does not exist in this pass.
